title: The IIT Delhi Engineer Behind Apple's Foldable iPhone Duo
excerpt: Piyush Pratik, an IIT Delhi graduate turned Apple product manager, holds a leadership role on the iPhone Duo — Apple's first foldable iPhone and its most expensive model ever.
body:
• Apple's first foldable iPhone, the iPhone Duo, was unveiled on September 9, 2026, with a 7.6-inch internal display and a 5.4-inch outer screen. It goes on sale at ₹2,99,900 from October 23.
  • Piyush Pratik, an IIT Delhi graduate from the 2011 batch, is a product manager at Apple whose LinkedIn profile lists his current role as Product Manager, iPhone Duo.
  • His path runs through Bain & Company, InMobi, and a Stanford GSB MBA on a Reliance Dhirubhai Fellowship before joining Apple in 2019, where he earlier worked on the iPhone 13 lineup, the second-generation iPhone SE, and the iPhone 16's Camera Control.
  • No single person builds an iPhone: hardware, software, design, camera, operations, and marketing teams share the work. Pratik's role puts him in the leadership team for the product, not sole credit for it.

The most expensive iPhone ever

Apple's iPhone Duo is the company's first foldable iPhone, unveiled at its September 9, 2026 event and named for its dual-screen folding form factor. Open it up and you get a 7.6-inch display; closed, a 5.4-inch outer screen handles everyday use. In India, the Duo starts at ₹2,99,900 — nearly three lakh rupees, making it the priciest iPhone Apple has ever sold — with sales beginning October 23.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=M-opQ80Nv4M

The phone has dominated tech conversation since the announcement, and for a reason that goes beyond the hinge: the product team behind it includes a prominent Indian name.

The Indian on the team

That name is Piyush Pratik. His LinkedIn profile lists his current position as Product Manager, iPhone Duo, and in a recent post he described leading the product as a great responsibility and a privilege, crediting the many Apple teams whose work went into it. He also called the Duo's launch one of the biggest changes to the iPhone since the original.

"Leading this product has been a great responsibility and a privilege."

— Piyush Pratik, Product Manager (iPhone Duo), Apple, via LinkedIn

Pratik's journey to Cupertino started at IIT Delhi, where he earned a dual B.Tech and M.Tech in biochemical engineering and biotechnology in 2011, reportedly graduating with a gold medal. His career did not follow the usual engineering track: he began as an associate consultant at Bain & Company, then joined InMobi in 2013, where he worked in product marketing and rose to director.

In 2017 he stepped away for an MBA at Stanford Graduate School of Business, funded by the Reliance Dhirubhai Scholarship, a fellowship open only to Indian citizens. He joined Apple in 2019 as an iPhone product manager, working on the iPhone 13 lineup and the second-generation iPhone SE before taking on a visible role at the iPhone 16 launch event in 2024, where he introduced the Camera Control button and its pressure-and-touch interface.

A correction worth making

The hype around Pratik should not overshadow how Apple products actually get built. An iPhone is the work of interlocking teams across hardware, software, industrial design, camera engineering, operations, and marketing — no one person, however senior, makes it alone. Calling Pratik "the Indian who made the iPhone Duo" would misstate his role. What his profile and his own words do establish is that he sits in the leadership team steering the product, with day-to-day responsibility for defining its features across engineering and design.

Why the diaspora is paying attention

Indian-origin engineers have long been a quiet force inside Silicon Valley hardware and software, but they rarely get a name and a stage. Pratik's turn at the iPhone 16 launch and now his visible role on Apple's most ambitious iPhone in a decade put an Indian face on one of the industry's flagship products. For the diaspora, the story lands because it mirrors a familiar arc: IIT classroom to global boardroom, via consulting and a Stanford detour.

What's next

The Duo reaches stores on October 23, and the real test begins there — whether foldable iPhones can justify their price tag beyond early adopters. Pratik, meanwhile, has one of the most scrutinized product portfolios at Apple. How the Duo sells will say as much about his leadership as about Apple's foldable bet.
